notable_absence.finding: The page names no Kubernetes-native object at all - no CustomResourceDefinition, StatefulSet, Helm chart, Service, or Operator CRD field is mentioned anywhere on this page. Every actual deployment mechanism is deferred to the operator/ tutorial ('Follow the instructions in this tutorial to connect Sync Gateway deployed on Kubernetes to a Couchbase Server cluster'), which is outside this round's file list. This page itself contributes only three facts: the CAO-1.2 mTLS limitation, the RBAC-user cross-reference, and a one-line framing of the topology - confirming the round-context hypothesis that install/deploy procedural content, including this first-contact Kubernetes page, would need relatively little new minting once the actual mechanism detail is out of scope.

cross_component_finding: This page is explicitly framed as a deviations list layered on top of a Couchbase Operator (Kubernetes) tutorial page (operator/current/tutorial-sync-gateway.md) rather than a self-contained procedure - every substantive instruction ('Deploying Sync Gateway', 'Configuring RBAC User for Sync Gateway', 'Enabling TLS Connectivity to Couchbase Server') is a named section anchor on that other page, not content here. Sync Gateway's own Kubernetes deployment story is therefore split across two different documentation module trees (sync-gateway/use-kubernetes/ and operator/), with this page acting purely as a thin, product-scoped index into the Operator tree's generic instructions plus two Sync-Gateway/CAO-version-specific caveats.
cross_product_finding: The page's only citation of a specific product version pairing is 'Couchbase Autonomous Operator 1.2' as the gating condition for the mTLS limitation - a Sync-Gateway-to-(Server-via-Operator) compatibility fact analogous in shape to get-started-prepare.md's Sync-Gateway-to-Couchbase-Server and Sync-Gateway-to-Couchbase-Lite version matrices (same batch), but expressed as a single prose deviation rather than a matrix.
